Recalls and safety alerts published in Canada, read from the open data of
Health Canada: food recalls of the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA),
consumer products, vehicles, tires and child car seats of Transport Canada,
drugs and health products, medical devices. The integration gives Gladys a
device with two values, a scene trigger for each new recall of your
selection, a scene action and a dashboard widget.

It was tested against the real file of Health Canada and in a test Gladys
(29/10/2026), not yet over weeks of real use. No device of yours is involved:
the data comes from the cloud.

## What you get

- A device **Recalls in Canada** with:
  - **Recalls in 7 days**: the sheets of your selection, not archived, whose
    "last updated" day is one of the last 7 days (today included, in the time
    zone of Gladys). The file gives no publication date: an older sheet
    updated this week counts too.
  - **Latest recall**: the newest of them, with its day.
- A scene trigger **Canada: new recall in my selection**, with the title,
  product, category, issue, recall class, link and a one-sentence summary as
  variables. The trigger can be limited to some categories.
- A scene action **Canada: read the recalls of the last 7 days** (a sentence
  to send by message or read aloud, and the count).
- A widget **Recalls in Canada**: the latest recalls of your selection, the
  most serious ones (Class 1, Type I) in red, with the link to each sheet.
- A button **Show the recalls of the last 7 days** in the configuration.

## Configuration

1. **Categories**: food (CFIA), consumer products, vehicles (Transport
   Canada), drugs and health products, medical devices, other. Medical
   devices are not followed by default: a quarter of the sheets, nearly all
   hospital and laboratory equipment.
2. **Brands or words** (optional): only the recalls naming one of them in
   their title, product or category, separated by commas. Accents and case do
   not matter; a word matches whole words only ("nut" does not match
   "peanut").
3. **Check interval**: 3, 6 (default), 12 or 24 hours.
4. **Language of the recalls**: English or French. It picks the file read
   (each language has its own), the names of the features at their creation
   and the texts sent to the scenes.

Save, then create the device in the **Discover** tab.

## How it works

Health Canada publishes one file per language (16 MB in English, 21 MB in
French, about 34,000 sheets since 1991), regenerated once a day around 02:15
UTC. At each check the integration asks whether the file changed
(`If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`): while it did not, the server
answers "not modified" and nothing is downloaded. When it changed, the file
is read as a stream: only the numbers (NID) of the sheets and the sheets of
the last 30 days stay in memory. One request at a time, with a User-Agent
naming the integration.

A recall is **new** when its number was absent from every file read before.
The first file ever read fires nothing (what is listed then is not news), nor
does a widened selection, nor a sheet only updated. A new sheet whose "last
updated" day is more than 7 days old is remembered without firing. A scene
event Gladys refuses is sent again at the next check; at most 20 events leave
per check, the rest at the next one. An event is sent before `/data` records
it: if the integration is killed in between, it is sent again after the
restart. Some new recalls are never sent, and the status says when the caps
are reached: beyond 500 new sheets in one file, beyond 500 events waiting,
or once their "last updated" day is more than 7 days old.

What was seen, the copy of the recent sheets and the time of the last check
are kept in `/data`: a restart fires nothing again, keeps the time planned
for the next check, and publishes the copy kept if it is still fresh.
Changing the selection is applied at once from the copy kept; changing the
language checks the other file (not twice in 5 minutes, never during a
pause). A copy of each language is kept, so going back costs a "not
modified". Configurations saved one after the other are applied in order:
the last one wins.

When a server of the content network still serves an older file than the
copy kept, the copy is kept and the next checks send only its date, so that
server answers "not modified" instead of sending 16 MB again. A file in
another format (fewer than half of the sheets dated, a column renamed) is
refused, never read as "no recall".

## Status and failures

The status of the integration says:

- the file cannot be read (network, HTTP error), with the next try: 15
  minutes later, then 30, doubled up to the interval; a "429" or "5xx" answer
  starts a pause of 1 minute to 6 hours (the server's `Retry-After` when it
  gives one), kept across restarts;
- the file has not changed for more than 3 days (compared to the date the
  server gives): the counters are then not published again until it changes,
  so an old value is not shown as fresh;
- no category is selected;
- `/data` cannot be read or written.

## Up to date or not

The recalls are **up to date** when the last successful check is less than
two intervals and an hour old and the file is not stale. Otherwise:

- the counters of the device are not published (they keep their last value);
- the scene action fails with the reason ("The recalls are not up to date:
  the file of Health Canada was last read on …" or "… has not changed since
  …"), so a scene never reads "no recall" from data that is not current;
- the configuration button gives that reason instead of the recalls;
- the widget titles "Recalls not up to date" and gives the reason under the
  list.

When the last check failed but the recalls are still up to date, the scene
action, the button and the widget give them with a warning first ("Warning:
the last check of the file failed …; the recalls are those read on …").

Nothing is published as 0 when the file could not be read.

## Limits

- A complement, not an official alert system: always check the recall sheet
  on [recalls-rappels.canada.ca](https://recalls-rappels.canada.ca/en). Not
  affiliated with the Government of Canada.
- The file holds no barcode (UPC) and no province: neither can be filtered.
- The file holds no publication date, only "last updated".

Health Canada). No account, no key, no personal data.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Rappels Canada asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your selection | `section` | No | Health Canada publishes every recall and safety alert of Canada as open data: food (CFIA), consumer products, vehicles (Transport Canada), drugs and health products, medical devices. Choose the categories to follow and, if you like, brands or words. Save, then create the device in the Discover tab. |
| Sources and limits | `section` | No | Data: "Recalls and safety alerts" of Health Canada, under the Open Government Licence – Canada, read without an account (one file of 16 to 21 MB, downloaded when it changes, about once a day). A complement, not an official alert system: always check the recall sheet. Not affiliated with the Government of Canada. |
| Categories | `multi_select` | No | Recalls and alerts of these categories are followed. About 35 a week (autumn 2026): 40 % vehicles, a quarter medical devices (not followed by default). |
| Brands or words (optional) | `string` | No | Only the recalls naming one of them (title, product or category), separated by commas. Accents and case do not matter. Empty: every recall of the categories. |
| Check interval | `select` | No | Health Canada regenerates the file once a day: a check of an unchanged file downloads nothing. |
| Language of the recalls | `select` | No | The file read (English or French), the names of the features (at their creation) and the texts sent to the scenes. |

## How to install Rappels Canada in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Rappels Canada appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-rappels-canada:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-rappels-canada](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-rappels-canada).

Rappels Canada requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Rappels Canada is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
